one_month_reasoning: Q3 FY26 results are most likely Wed 2026-10-28, inside the window. FORM has reported on a Wednesday every quarter (Q3 releases on 2024-10-30 and 2025-10-29), and the Nov 4 calendar date matches last year's 10-Q filing, not the release. No 8-K has been filed since the Q2 release, so the date is unconfirmed. I put it at about 85-90% inside the window. Q3 should beat the $270M / $0.86 guide again, since the last two quarters beat the top of the range. But the Q3 numbers include $7-9M of IEEPA tariff refunds (10-Q) and other one-offs worth about 300bp of GM, which disappear in the Q4 guide. Farmers Branch start-up costs (already inside non-GAAP opex, $4.9M in Q2) move into COGS as production starts late in Q4. So the Q4 margin guide will likely step down even on higher revenue. After a 55% one-month run on one sell-side note, those two forces roughly cancel. I centre on spot (about $148.6, against the $149.15 actual 10/2 close) with a lognormal one-month sigma of 0.21, roughly 85%/3.5 trimmed slightly. That is near-symmetric with no directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM (Oct 2027) non-GAAP EPS $4.35 x 30x plus $5.4/sh net cash ($136, 60%), NTM revenue $1.38B x 7x EV/sales ($125, 20%) and FY2028 FCF $290M at a 3% yield ($126, 20%). EPS is rebuilt from a clean Q3 run rate of about $0.77 that excludes the one-off tariff refunds and metal reclaims; the blend is about $132.

The start-up costs are therefore already in the run rate; moving them into COGS as production starts late in Q4 FY26 lowers reported GM but is roughly neutral to EPS, apart from under-absorption during the FY27 ramp.

Revenue $1.25B (Q3 run rate about $1.1B, +about 15% on HBM4, Foundry & Logic and CPO, held back by Technoprobe's faster growth); underlying GM 51.5% (51% clean baseline plus restructuring savings, minus Farmers Branch under-absorption); non-GAAP opex about $290M (Q2 $65.7M/qtr growing); interest plus equity income about $18M; 15% tax; 80.5M shares

Revenue about $1.40B, GM about 53% as Farmers Branch reaches target levels (10-Q: 'more favorable cost structure overall, once ramped'), opex about $310M, 15% tax, 81M shares gives about $4.8. I haircut that to $4.50 for memory-capex cyclicality (SK hynix 24% of Q2 revenue) and Technoprobe share pressure. The SA contributor's $4.25 is a newsletter cross-check, not sell-side.

DB's $200 target and the SA contributor's 40x mark the bullish end. At $149 the stock is about 48x the clean run rate and about 38x FY27E. I assume compression to 30x as growth normalizes from more than 30% toward about 15%, and because these are near-peak margins in a cyclical business.

$109.8M cash + $235.9M securities - about $11.6M debt = $334M at 6/27/26, plus about $100M+ of FCF over five quarters after the Farmers Branch capex (buyback paused; $70.9M authorization left), over about 81M shares

bear.story: Memory/HBM capex digestion in 2027 (SK hynix is 24% of Q2 revenue, 29.5% in Q1), Technoprobe takes HBM4 and GPU share, the Nvidia second source stays small, and the Farmers Branch ramp under-absorbs, leaving GM near 50%. FY28 EPS stalls near $3.6 at about 21x. That would be a roughly 50% drawdown, which matches FORM's two roughly 60% peak-to-trough falls in the last five years and the 49% drop within 2026.

base.story: Beat-and-raise continues on clean margins. FY27 revenue is about $1.25B and EPS about $3.90, with NTM EPS of about $4.35 by Oct 2027 at about 31x plus cash. Earnings grow about 40% from the clean run rate, but the multiple compresses from about 48x clean to about 31x, so the stock ends slightly below today's price.

bull.story: The Nvidia GPU second source at TSMC ramps (Nvidia was already a 10.2% customer in Q1 2026), HBM4 share holds against Technoprobe, CPO systems grow, and Farmers Branch brings GM to about 55% by 2028. FY28 EPS of about $5.6 holds about 38x plus cash.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $92 (the early-September low, about 38% under the $149 spot), the stock would be pricing about 21x a clean NTM EPS of about $4.35, a multiple FORM has only held on trough expectations. Getting there would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility: an HBM/DRAM order cut at SK hynix or Micron, visible HBM4 or GPU share loss to Technoprobe, the Nvidia/TSMC second source failing to convert, or underlying GM settling below about 51% once Farmers Branch costs reach COGS.

reasoning: Round 2. I accept the supervisor's main correction and checked it in the 10-Q myself. FORM expects $7.0-9.0M of IEEPA tariff refunds in Q3 FY26, and only $0.8M had been received by 6/27. With metal reclaims, about 300bp of the 54% non-GAAP GM guide is one-off, so the clean Q3 run rate is about $0.77, not $0.86. My round-1 FY28 EPS of $4.75 compounded that inflated margin. One new primary finding: the Q2 non-GAAP reconciliation does not exclude factory start-up costs ($4.9M Q2, $11.9M 1H). So when those costs move into COGS, reported GM falls but EPS barely changes, and I do not double-count them as a further hit. I rebuilt the EPS line from the clean base: FY27E $3.90 and FY28E $4.50, for an NTM of about $4.35 at Oct 2027. The supervisor gets about $4.30 by a different route. Methods: P/E $136 (60%), EV/sales $125 (20%) and FCF yield $126 (20%), blended to $132, down from $141. I now treat the $4.25 / 40x figure as a Seeking Alpha contributor's (newsletter), not an analyst's. I also add the primary support for the Nvidia link (10.2% customer in Q1 2026), but I still count DB's >$200M claim only in the bull case. The supervisor's drawdown check (two roughly 60% falls on weekly closes, -49% within 2026) supports a fat left tail, so the bear case is $78 at 27%. Scenarios: $78/27%, $140/45%, $225/28%, with a mean of about $147 and a median of about $140. For the ladder I mixed a lognormal (median $141, sigma 0.58) with the bear and bull lumps (25%). That puts P(>=148) at 0.47 (from 0.50) and trims every strike above $133 by 2-3 points. I disagree mildly with the supervisor on Q2 margin: Q2 (53.3%) had almost no refund benefit, so underlying GM may be closer to 52-53% than 51%. That is why my FY27 GM is 51.5% rather than 51%. I used 8-K/10-Q/EDGAR primary sources; the research was limited to about 4 fetches.
